name: Sindhi Topi
basis: why: a cap embroidered in rings of triangles, diamonds and tiny mirrors; how: polar rings of cells in thread colours, rings of mirrors
note: Mirrors are one of four ring ornaments; the filled cells stand for satin-type stitches. Could be its own stitch page.

lumenary.blurb: The embroidered cap of Sindh seen from above: rings of triangles, diamonds and tiny mirrors around a central disc, each stitched in a colour taken from your picture.

facts.era: Traditional, worn today at weddings and on Sindhi Cultural Day

why: The Sindhi topi is a round cap with a notch cut for the forehead, embroidered all over in rings of triangles, diamonds and tiny mirrors. Seen from above, the rings are circles and the pattern is easiest to read, so that is how the program draws it. Each cell is stitched in a colour taken from your picture, like a small mosaic of thread.
how: Make K rings between an inner radius r₀ = 0.11 R and 0.96 R, each of width h = (0.96 R − r₀)/K.
Let four kinds of ornament take turns going outward: triangles, diamonds, zigzags and mirrors.
Cut each ring into n cells, with n = 2 ⌈(2π ρ / (c h)) / 2⌉, where ρ is the ring’s middle radius and c the cell shape slider, so n is always even and triangles can alternate pointing out and in.
Turn odd rings by half a cell, as in real caps.
Choose each cell’s colour from the eight thread colours of the topi, matched to the picture, with the ground of each ring alternating between cream and black.
history: The Sindhi topi is worn with the ajrak at weddings, at festivals and on Sindhi Cultural Day, celebrated on the first Sunday of December. The notch is often explained as letting the forehead touch the ground in prayer. Caps are embroidered and sewn by hand by makers in towns and villages across Sindh.
terms: A cap, in several South Asian languages.
A band of pattern around the centre of the cap.

paragraphs: The Sindhi topi is a round cap with a notch cut for the forehead. It is embroidered all over in rings of triangles, diamonds and tiny mirrors, and it is worn with the ajrak at weddings and on Sindhi Cultural Day. The program draws it as if you were looking down on the crown, where the rings are circles and the pattern is easiest to see. There are K rings between an inner radius r₀ = 0.11 R and 0.96 R, each of width h = (0.96 R − r₀)/K, and four kinds of ornament take turns going outward: triangles, diamonds, zigzags and mirrors.

Each ring is cut into n cells, with n = 2 ⌈(2π ρ / (c h)) / 2⌉, where ρ is the ring’s middle radius and c the cell shape slider. n is always even so triangles can alternate pointing out and in. Odd rings are turned by half a cell, as in real caps. A cell’s colour is chosen from the eight thread colours of the topi by finding the nearest to the picture’s (saturated) colour at the middle of the cell. The ground of the ring alternates between cream and black. In the centre a ring of twelve petals surrounds a larger mirror, and the edge is a scalloped rim of round beads.

equations.note: Ring width and the middle radius of ring k (k = 0 is innermost).
Number of cells in ring k, made even, and the start angle of cell j. Odd rings are shifted by half a cell.
The order of ornaments from the centre outward.
The beads on the rim are a little larger than half their spacing, so they overlap into a scallop.

presets.text: More rings give a finer and busier cap.
Maroon cloth with mirrors on looks festive.
Wider cells make bold, chunky ornaments.
